key_insight: This study compares eight approaches to missing covariates, from traditional statistics to deep learning, to inform method selection in Alzheimer’s disease research.
clinical_relevance: Handling missing biomarkers appropriately matters for interpreting Alzheimer’s research, especially when measurements are costly or invasive to obtain.
method: Compare complete-case analysis, multiple imputation, and machine learning methods.
Evaluate deep learning frameworks including multilayer perceptrons, variational autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks.
Assess regression estimates across missingness mechanisms and proportions.
evidence_signal: Simulations assess bias, efficiency, standard error accuracy, confidence interval coverage, and computational burden, alongside an application to the Vanderbilt Memory and Aging Project.
watch_item: The abstract reports no comparative results, so it does not establish a best-performing method.
paper_title: Statistical, Machine Learning and Deep Learning Methods for Missing Covariates: An Empirical Evaluation with Applications to Alzheimer's Disease Research
